title: Failure of translation stability
statement: For any real numbers $b,B$ with $1<b<B$, there exist a probability distribution $p$ on $\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and a function $X:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\to\mathbb R$ such that $1\le b$ and $\mathbb E_p[X^4]\le b\,\mathbb E_p[X^2]^2$, but the function $1+X$ does not satisfy both $1\le B$ and $\mathbb E_p[(1+X)^4]\le B\,\mathbb E_p[(1+X)^2]^2$.
hypotheses_covered: there exist a probability mass function on the two-element set and a real-valued function on that set
